gen-gf-revalia-manrope: Manrope opens with bright gaps in every curve and a line that never changes width, while Revalia stomps in above it, bold and widely spaced. They make a lively, loose-limbed pair.
gen-gf-snowburst-one-montserrat: Cut like stencil. Snowburst One sits tall and bold up top, while Montserrat glides underneath, its curves wide open and its sans lines smooth.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips well apart and its strokes steady. Ethnocentric looks fast and pushy above it, so give that heading plenty of size and let it run wide.
gen-gf-underdog-fs-bespoke-sans: Rounded, wide-mouthed and loud. Underdog carries a horseshoe c with no swelling, while Bespoke Sans follows with sharp, refined lines and generous room between curve ends and stems.
gen-gf-unica-one-archivo: Archivo has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, so text moves along easily. And Unica One adds a very large lowercase with daylight inside every curve.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-satoshi: Gaps split every word into single letters. Electroharmonix earns its keep when the words are big and short, and Satoshi gives the text a soaring x-height beneath it.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-asap: Tapered ink and stretched spacing, all at one stroke width. Asap sits beneath with open arcs and a body height nearly matching the capitals, so the text feels sturdy.
gen-eater-switzer: Switzer reads like wire, with tubular letters, a tall waist line and a constant weight tracing every shape. And Eater adds dark, wide-gapped menace above it.
gen-dafont-woodgod-work-sans: Woodgod brings a vintage, commanding look, with a wide channel into every bowl and tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Work Sans follows with modern, bent-wire lines and tips kept apart.
gen-gf-autour-one-general-sans: Round, bold and a little showy. Autour One leads with clear channels into each curve, and General Sans matches its smooth bends with a tall x-height and steady pressure.
